# Kalimat

> Kalimat (كلمات, "words") is a free, browser-based Arabic vocabulary trainer for beginners, made by Ummah Apps. URL: https://kalimat.ummahapps.ai/

## What it does

- Over 400 everyday Modern Standard Arabic words in 16 groups: basics, people, places, home and school, food and drink, nature and animals, body, colours, describing words, actions (past-tense verbs), numbers, time and days, greetings, clothes, toys and play, feelings.
- Every word is written with full harakat (vowel marks) and has an English meaning.
- Words are spoken aloud using the device's text-to-speech voice, at normal or slow speed.
- Most nouns and describing words show their plural, labelled as a sound plural or broken plural.
- Words are sorted from Beginner to Intermediate to Advanced, with a level filter remembered for each learner.
- Qur'an words: a second word list with the most common words in the Qur'an, from the booklet "80% of Qur'anic Words" by Dr Abdulazeez Abdulraheem. Words in both lists show both meanings.
- Verbs show their five forms (past, present, command, doer, action noun).
- Stories: 10 short, fully vowelled stories made mostly from words in Kalimat. Listen first with pictures, read along and tap any word for its meaning, answer questions in Arabic, then tell the story yourself. Each story shows how many of its words you already know, suggests a good next story and offers to add its new words to Learning.
- Games: "pick the picture" (match the Arabic word to its sketch), "pick the plural" (choose the right plural of a word, with hints about sound and broken plurals), "pick the form" (choose the right verb form), "say it from memory", "say the plural from memory", and "revise known words", which quizzes Known well words in both directions. An optional timer (10 or 20 seconds) can be switched on.
- Every word has a pencil sketch, shown on the cards and in the games.
- A "My Learning words" button shows only the words being practised.
- Progress tracking: mark the words you are learning, then mark them as known well. A word moves to Known well by itself after 5 right-first-time answers in a row in the games or story questions. Known well words come back for spaced checks (after 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, then 2 months; a wrong answer brings the word back the next day).
- Learners can add their own words, with plurals and groups.
- A short plain-English note explains sound plurals (ـُونَ / ـِينَ and ـَات) and broken plurals (كِتَاب ← كُتُب).
- Learners are shared with the sister apps Takallum Kids, Kalimat Plus and Takallum on the same device, and words already known in those apps can be added to Learning in one tap.
- Up to three learners can share one device, each with their own progress.
- Free, no account, no ads. Progress is stored only in the learner's browser.

## Who it is for

Beginners of any age learning Arabic: children, home-schooling families, and adults in Quranic or Madinah-style Arabic classes.
